desk.headline: HEPS down 14% to 406.8c on flat revenue of R4.29bn; dividend cut 9% to 413c; sees strong stock-picking opportunities
results: Headline earnings per share fell 14% to 406.8c; fund management earnings per share, the core measure, fell about 9% to 413.7c.
Revenue was flat at about R4.29bn even though average assets under management rose 10% to R774bn; costs rose, but by less than inflation.
Closing assets slipped 1% to R750bn; net outflows eased significantly compared with the year before.
Second-half fund management EPS of about 210c was above the first half's 203.7c, which the company called positive momentum.
Final dividend of 210.0c (prior 254.0c) takes the year's total to 413.0c, down from 454.0c.

guidance.summary: Coronation gives no earnings or flow targets. It describes the outlook: short-term performance has been hard, but it sees outstanding stock-picking chances in South Africa and abroad, while weak economic growth keeps weighing on industry savings flows.

points: Management called short-term investment performance challenging but said the market suits patient, active stock pickers.
In South Africa it sees precious-metal shares as fully priced, but other valuations as very attractive.
Globally it views AI "picks and shovels" companies as overvalued and prefers quality firms that will use AI to cut costs.
It says industry flows need stronger economic growth, as structural problems keep squeezing household saving.
call.source: Business Day coverage of the results commentary (17 Nov 2026)

watch: Whether second-half earnings momentum carries into FY2027 as average assets stay high.
Net flows: outflows have eased, but the company links a lasting recovery to stronger economic growth.
Whether the portfolio tilts away from gold and AI infrastructure stocks pay off in relative performance.
